The scent of crayons and slightly-too-sweet hand sanitizer was the first thing Eleanor noticed every Tuesday and Thursday morning. It was the smell of Mrs. Davison’s second-grade classroom at Maplewood Elementary, and it was a smell Eleanor had come to cherish. For the past two years, she’d been a volunteer classroom aide, and it had quietly, profoundly, changed her life.

Eleanor, a retired librarian, had initially signed up to fill the time. Her husband, Arthur, had passed away the previous spring, leaving a gaping hole in her days. The quiet of her house had become oppressive, the silence a constant reminder of his absence. Her daughter, Sarah, had gently suggested volunteering, hoping it would bring Eleanor some purpose.

And it had.
